subject.title: v2026.6.x system prompt bloat causes instruction following degradation on smaller models

question: Should OpenClaw treat this smaller-model prompt/skill priority regression as a coordinated core prompt-budget/defaults project now, and which existing tracker or implementation path should own it?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent fix could alter config defaults, prompt sections, skill loading, or context compaction policy, and those are product/compatibility choices rather than a narrow code repair.

options.title: Coordinate the existing trackers
options.body: Use this issue as evidence for the existing prompt-pressure cluster and decide across https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/75189, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90349, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/22438 before changing defaults or prompt priority.

options.title: Narrow to opt-in guidance only
options.body: Keep current defaults and improve documentation/doctor guidance around localModelLean, bootstrap budgets, and skills limits without changing runtime behavior yet.

options.title: Decline as model limitation
options.body: Close the product direction by documenting that weaker models need operator-selected lean profiles or stronger providers, accepting that this report remains outside core guarantees.

recommendation.title: Coordinate the existing trackers
recommendation.body: Use this issue as evidence for the existing prompt-pressure cluster and decide across https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/75189, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90349, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/22438 before changing defaults or prompt priority.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans product defaults, prompt context policy, and related open tracker routing, and this account has the strongest recent runtime/defaults review signal among the related owners.
